scope: [which milestone / slice this contract governs — a contract covers one build, not the whole roadmap]
authoredBy: [session/agent that wrote this — MUST NOT be the one that implements it]
sourceDocs: [requirements doc the assertions were derived from — NOT the implementation]
_comment_pinnedValues: Decisions frozen so they cannot silently drift. SLOs, caps, vendors, budgets, chosen technologies. If an implementation wants to change one of these, that is an escalation, not a refactor.

pinnedValues.[exampleSLO]: <= 60 minutes from failure visible to alert dispatch
pinnedValues.[exampleChoice]: DuckDB, not SQLite — workload is analytical

_comment_gradingRule: Copy verbatim from METHODOLOGY.md section 2. Do not soften it. The two negative clauses do most of the work.
gradingRule: An independent EVALUATOR assumes the build is broken and must prove each MUST assertion PASS with concrete, reproducible evidence (a passing automated test, a captured trace with correlation IDs, or a live reproduction) — NOT 'code review' as standalone evidence, and NOT a recorded/replayed fixture where the assertion demands live behavior. Ship requires every MUST to PASS; SHOULDs are tracked; MUST-NOT assertions must be shown absent by an enumerable check (enum/registry membership, grep, or module-boundary gate).
_comment_nonGoals: The scope fence. Prevents an evaluator filing findings against features never promised, and prevents a builder gold-plating. Be specific.
nonGoals_v1: [thing deliberately not built in this slice]
[thing deferred to a later version, named]
_comment_assertions: Each MUST is a failing test you have not written yet. If you cannot name the evidence in `verify`, the assertion is too vague to build against — rewrite it. Weight the contract toward assertions where being wrong is EXPENSIVE and SILENT (isolation, authorization, data loss, money), not toward what is easiest to assert.

assertions.assertion: [A single falsifiable claim about system behavior. Present tense. One claim, not three.]
assertions.verify: [The specific evidence that settles it. Which test, which trace, which live reproduction. Include the mutation check: 'remove X and assert this test goes red.']

assertions.assertion: [Something that must never occur — a credential in a log, a cross-tenant read, a direct import across a module boundary.]
assertions.verify: [An ENUMERABLE check. A grep, a module-graph gate, enum membership. 'I did not see one' is not enumerable and does not count.]
